new_findings.text: The build-parity trap this packet flags for CRIT_MULT is not a one-off; the android damage and reach tuning diverges from web across the board, so the android blobs are unsafe as a source for ANY combat number. Reading the two twins side by side: DAMAGE - web §1t99s0§.as:3262 Light '_loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android MCSPlayer.as:3205 'baseDamage * (0.5 + 0.5 * lightMastery * 0.01)'; web :3265 Balanced '(1 + 0.2 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android :3208 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'; web :3270 Heavy '_loc1_ * 1.4' vs android :3213 'baseDamage * 1.5'. REACH - web :3094 Light 'this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4' vs android :3030 'this.baseSlashLength * 1.5'; web :3105 Balanced '(1 + 0.2 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android :3041 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'. METER - web max 192 vs android 120; web stance-switch cost a flat 48 vs android proportional (maxreload/3 or -maxreload/6). Every one of these is a number a ledger row could be built on. The mastery terms are not even the same shape: web multiplies mastery by 0.1, android by 0.01, so the two builds' mastery curves are on different scales and a value 'confirmed' in one is meaningless in the other.

new_findings.text: THE STAGE-PX-TO-FRAME-PX CONVERSION THE CORPUS USES IS RIGHT ON ONE AXIS ONLY. new_findings.text: One packet finding closed RR:190 blocker ① 'in STAGE PIXELS' and the other explicitly held the unit question open ('What is NOT closed: the unit-to-stage-px scale factor, which still wants one frame measurement'). The open half is closed, and not from the inventory text — from the input path that consumes the number. MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094 passes the freshly computed slashLength straight into InputManager.setMaxDistance, InputManager.as:106-108 stores it as maxDistance, and :198 loads distanceLeft = maxDistance at mouse-down. The drawn blade path then spends that budget in Euclidean units of the DESCALED stage space: :342-343 compute mouseX/mouseY as (stageMC.mouseX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale, :355 takes the squared distance between consecutive descaled points, and :367 subtracts it from distanceLeft. That coordinate space is the native game stage — :348 bounds it by StatsManager.stageWidth/stageHeight and :231 rejects any release with mouseY > 480, the literal native height. So slashLength is a length in native 800x480 stage pixels by construction, no scale factor outstanding: a 1080p capture is that space times 1080/480 = 2.25 (before pillarbox). No frame measurement is needed, and none should be commissioned.

RR:90-91 lists 'the SPEED-stat->cooldown formula' as a KNOWN-UNKNOWN, and RR:200 progression blocker ① asks to measure 'SPD range/cooldown scaling ... per-point deltas in a build'. The formula is in web v0.717 source, two functions below the slash-length one. §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2296 is 'if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5;' and its caller applies the same SPD + gear-bonus + x1.5-speed-buff preamble the slash-length getter uses. It is displayed to the player as '0.xxx' next to slash distance (web §1t5957s0§.as:3014 getString(983) + int(modifier * 1000); android InventoryUI.as:2233 'skill cooldown modifier: '). new_findings.text: A BUILD LEAK INSIDE A SURVIVING FINDING, EXACTLY THE C2 TRAP. LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:3644, [[ui-hud/in-combat-hud-is-three-bars]], says 'The third bar carries the status text CANNOT CHANGE STANCE when it is below a sixth of max.' A SIXTH is the ANDROID rule: MCSPlayer.as:2977 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) return;' over maxreload = 5 * 24 = 120 (:239), i.e. 20. The WEB build has no sixth anywhere in this path: §1t113s0§.as:328 draws the bar as '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' and shows the grey caption only at ratio == 0 (:336-343), over maxreload = 8 * 24 = 192 (§1t99s0§.as:249) — so the caption is on while reload <= 48, a QUARTER of max, and the threshold is the same flat 48 the stance gate uses (:3050, :3060). The finding names no build, which under §3(c) makes it the defective side rather than a genuine contradiction. Consequence if shipped as written: on a 192-tick meter the caption would clear at 32 instead of 48, and a stance switch would be offered for 16 ticks while the code still refuses it — the one visible state the whole cluster exists to reproduce.

The value is web-side too. §1t1523s0§.as:2346-2347 computes base slash length as 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));' — identical to android getBaseSlashLengthVal at StatsManager.as:1915-1919 — where param1 is SPEED (×1.5 under the speed buff) and §1t9426s0§ is the Dan/rebirth stat. At Dan 0 the base runs 120 stage px (speed 0) asymptotically to 210. Combined with the per-stance multipliers, the whole reach model is computable with no footage measurement.

new_findings.text: Found while checking nf1/nf2/nf3 in the same switch. The per-stance REACH table in §1t99s0§.as:3091-3155 is the mirror of the DAMAGE table at :3259-3271, and the ledger's 300/200/100 ordering is explained by it. Light (§1t12220s0§): damage ×(0.5+0.04·mLight) but reach ×1.4 FIXED (:3094). Balanced (§1t12221s0§): damage and reach BOTH ×(1+0.02·mBal) (:3105, :3265). Heavy (§1t12222s0§): damage ×1.4 fixed but reach ×(0.5+0.04·mHeavy) with a hard 100 px floor (:3116-3120). Two further stance ids exist: §1t12223s0§ reach = base with the same 100 floor (:3142-3146) and §1t12224s0§ reach ×1.4 (:3131). So the stance that hits hardest reaches shortest, and each stance's reach is governed by its OWN mastery, not a shared one.
